name: Monza 1937
notes: The Autodromo Nazionale di Monza, built inside the royal park north-east of Milan in 1922 and combining a road course with a banked high-speed ring into a full circuit of some ten kilometres. It was the fastest permanent autodrome in Europe and the most punishing: the 1933 Monza Grand Prix killed Giuseppe Campari, Baconin Borzacchini and Stanislas Czaykowski on the same oiled banking in a single afternoon, and the organisers spent the rest of the decade breaking the straights up with artificial chicanes to hold the speeds down. This is a pre-war dressing of the circuit.
author: Legion, Rainmaker
